# RustyNES v2.7.3 — "Hearth"

The fourth release of the audit line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put between v2.6.23 and the SuperStation One core (**v3.0.0**). It works from the frontend audit in [`docs/audits/`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/README.md), and its subject is the desktop and web frontends: they now keep what they are given, a save, a sound device, a script's limits, a window that stays responsive.

Every audit claim was checked against the code before anything changed. Most held. Three did not hold as written, and one bypass worse than any reported was found along the way; all are recorded in the [frontend ledger](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/frontend-disposition.md). The emulation core changes only by one additive accessor, and **AccuracyCoin 144/144** and **nestest** were re-measured on the release tree regardless. The full `--features test-roms` workspace suite passes **2,698 tests, 0 failed (v2.7.2: 2,666)**.

**The MiSTer sibling does not change in this release, and no new bitstream is cut.** No hardware has run any bitstream; the board session is v2.9.2.

## Battery saves on the desktop

Until this release the desktop kept no in-game save at all. Nothing in the frontend read the cartridge's battery RAM, so a game saved in-game, quit and relaunched came back with the save gone; it survived only inside a save state. The libretro core was never affected, since RetroArch keeps the `.srm` itself.

A battery-backed cartridge now keeps its save in `<data_dir>/battery/<rom-sha256>.sav`. It is loaded when the ROM loads, before the first frame, and written when it changes: compared once a second while running, and always on a ROM switch, close and exit. Four rules shape it:

- **Only a cartridge whose header sets the battery bit** is persisted. The save RAM slice is not that question: NROM, MMC1 and MMC3 expose work RAM whatever the header says, and keying on it would give volatile cartridges saves they never had. A new additive `Nes::has_battery()` answers it.
- **The file is keyed like save states**, by the ROM's full-file hash.
- **There is no core dirty flag.** The frontend compares against the bytes it last wrote, so a game that uses its battery RAM as scratch memory costs one write a second.
- **A save that was not read is never overwritten.** A file that cannot be read, or whose size is not the cartridge's, is left untouched, that session is not persisted, and the status bar says so. The size is checked before the file is read.

One interaction is recorded rather than changed: a power-on movie inherits a loaded `.sav`, because a power cycle does not clear cartridge RAM. That was already true within a session.

## A Lua script can no longer hang or exhaust the emulator

The per-frame instruction budget is a VM hook that raises an ordinary Lua error, and `pcall`, `xpcall` and `coroutine.resume` catch ordinary errors. A runaway loop wrapped in any of them caught its own abort and ran forever, holding the emulator lock. The sandbox now replaces those three with wrappers that re-raise once the budget has tripped, so the abort escapes any nesting, while ordinary errors are still caught.

Fixing that exposed something worse, which the audit had not reported: **a coroutine had no budget at all.** The hook was bound to the main thread, and the Lua binding removed it inside every coroutine, so a plain loop in a coroutine ran unbounded. It is now a global hook, copied into every coroutine, and it now also covers the callbacks the emulator fires itself (reset, sprite-zero hit, code breakpoints and the TAStudio events), which had never had a budget. The script heap is also capped at 64 MiB, and log output, which is held outside that heap, at 8,192 lines a frame of up to 4 KiB each.

## Script HTTP cannot reach the machine's own services

With the opt-in `script-ipc` feature, `comm.httpGet` and `comm.httpPost` fetched any URL, including loopback services and cloud metadata. Addresses that resolve to loopback, private, link-local and similar ranges now need the host listed in `RUSTYNES_COMM_HTTP_ALLOW` (for example `localhost:8080`), so a local bot endpoint stays one line of configuration away. The check runs in the HTTP client's resolver, on the addresses it actually connects to, so a name that answers differently to a second lookup gains nothing. Redirects are returned to the script instead of followed, closing a hop past the check that the audit did not mention. So is a proxy from `HTTP_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY`, which would resolve the target where the check cannot see it; script HTTP ignores the environment proxy. [ADR 0016](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0016-host-mediated-script-ipc.md) is amended with the policy. The audit's other half, unbounded response buffering, did not hold: the HTTP client already capped bodies at 10 MB. The cap is now stated explicitly.

## Input, audio and the window

- **One key no longer does three things.** `M` toggled the menu bar, held the Famicom microphone and pressed P3 Select at once, and P2 Select and P3 Right were both `L`. The audit named three of these; a test that checks every default binding found the fourth. The microphone is now held on `N`, P3 Select is `,` and P2 Select is `R`. Saved bindings are kept.
- **Audio comes back after the output device goes away.** An unplug, a Bluetooth drop or an audio-server restart used to leave the emulator silent until restart. The stream is reopened over the same buffer within about two seconds, so nothing else has to be restarted. If the device that answers is a different one, its own channel layout is used.
- **No periodic clicks at low latency on large-period devices.** The audit's example did not reproduce: a timeline simulation of a 20 ms target against a 1024-frame device period measured no underruns. A related case did: with a period of at least twice the target (2048 frames at 20 ms), rate control held the buffer below one device callback and it underran about once a second. The latency target now never drops below two device callbacks.
- **The debugger's text no longer turns to garbage after a skipped frame.** egui sends each font and image upload once; a frame whose swapchain image could not be acquired used to discard them, with the debugger or a tool panel open.
- **Fast-forward no longer floods the UI thread**, which received one wakeup per fast-forwarded frame. At most one is pending now. At normal speed, and whenever RetroAchievements is active, every frame still gets its own, because RetroAchievements is driven once per wakeup.
- **Stopping an A/V recording no longer freezes the window** for the length of the ffmpeg encode. It finishes in the background and completes before a quit.

## Web, HD packs and configuration

- The web canvas shrinks to fit a phone screen, and the audio worklet's temporary script URL is released once loaded.
- An HD pack can no longer exhaust memory: a PNG's declared size was trusted when sizing its decode buffer. Images past 16384 pixels a side or 4096 x 4096 in total are refused before anything is allocated, and a whole pack may decode at most 1 GiB of images. Its music can no longer claim an absurd sample rate either; a 1 Hz header expanded the track 48,000-fold.
- Achievement badges from earlier games are released when another ROM loads.
- Building the web frontend with both `wasm-canvas` and `wasm-winit` now stops at compile time with the right invocation.
- The `[retroachievements] host` setting is removed. Nothing ever read it; files that still contain it load unchanged.

| AccuracyCoin (RAM decoder) | 144 / 144, 0 fail, 0 not run |
| nestest | pass |
| `--features test-roms` workspace suite | 154 suites, 2,698 passed, 0 failed, 20 ignored |

| fmt, clippy (default, `scripting,hd-pack`, `retroachievements`, `av-record`, `script-ipc`, `full`, both wasm32), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `no_std` build | clean |
| Red first | where the defect was observable through an existing interface, its test was run against the unfixed code first: the Lua `pcall` and coroutine cases hung until killed, the 128 MiB script allocation succeeded, the over-size PNG decoded, the key-binding test listed exactly the four clashes, and the DESK-05 simulation counted 4 underruns |
| Mutations | run for battery saves (6 / 6, an out-of-memory kill counting as caught), the Lua sandbox (8 / 8, a hang counting as caught), script HTTP (7 / 7), audio device layout (3 / 3), HD-pack total budget (4 / 4), the PNG budget, fast-forward wakeups, audio reopen pacing (2 / 2) and badge clearing (3 / 3), all caught. Three are expected not to be caught and say so at the site: the second clear of the Lua budget flag, which the arming step repeats; the explicit HTTP body cap, which equals the client's own default, and either half of the DESK-05 fix alone, since each prevents the underruns by itself in the simulation |

**Not under automated test**, and verified by reading instead: the egui texture ordering (needs a GPU), the audio reopen (needs a device), the responsive canvas (not yet seen on a narrow screen), the worklet URL revoke, and the background A/V finalize (needs a window and ffmpeg). The ledger records each.

**Next:** v2.7.4 is the mobile release, including battery saves on Android and iOS.
